newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Distribution of LPG back to normal following settlement of last week's strike at Shell Gas Lanka Limited, the country's monopoly gas supplier. Employees struck work for six days due to a dispute over transfers and dismissals.
Sri Lanka's President Chandrika Kumaratunga calls for firm stand on terrorism, drug trafficking and illegal arms trade, at on-going SAARC summit in Maldives.
President Kumaratunga calls for critical analysis of progress of SAARC, which has pledged to eradicate poverty in the region in the next decade.
Sixteen policemen killed in Monday's Tamil Tiger separatist (LTTE) attack on Morawewa police station, in the northeast.

The main opposition United National Party (UNP) leader Ranil Wickremesinghe says he is ready to fight an election at any level. The UNP fared badly in the recent local government elections, where the ruling People's Alliance coalition won over 75 percent of the seats on offer.
President Kumaratunga calls upon SAARC leaders to join hands to eradicate terrorism, durg trafficking and illegal arms trade.
